subject: Hosted onramp fastpath: ops agreement & next steps
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Evan Li <evan.li@streamlineai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted onramp fastpath: ops agreement & next steps

Hi Evan / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Per our call, this thread is a concise ops-level agreement so Streamline.AI can evaluate Redwood Hosted quickly and safely. Below is a short summary of what we recommend for the pilot plus concrete next steps.

Summary (recommendation)
- Pilot on Redwood Hosted API (sandbox -> prod) to validate latency and prompt quality before considering Dedicated or Private. Hosted gives fastest time-to-value and built-in fallbacks.
- If you reach sustained production load above ~300 req/s or require VPC-only access, we can map a Dedicated path; Private (VPC/on-prem) remains an option for compliance-heavy workloads later.

Technical pilot profile (what we’ll provision)
- Sandbox endpoint: sandbox.streamline.redwood.ai (test keys, no billing).
- Prod endpoint mapping: api.streamline.redwood.ai (will map when ready).
- Baseline rate limits: 50 req/s per endpoint with burst up to 150 req/s for 10s windows; token caps set per model (default 2M tokens/day for pilot).
- KV/prefix caching: enabled for prompt prefix reuse; we’ll provide recommended cache TTLs in the pilot config.
- Canary routing: we suggest 5% traffic for 48 hours, then 25% for 72 hours before full cutover.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to smaller model family on overload; we’ll provide explicit policy for critical endpoints.

Compliance & data handling
- SOC 2 report and data-retention extract available (link below). Hosted keeps customer data isolated per-account; we can configure log retention to 30/90/365 days per your needs.

Immediate next steps (action items)
1) We’ll attach a pilot-config-template.xlsx and a draft SOW for your ops team to review (attached). Please fill in estimated concurrent users and peak QPS by Monday.
2) Redwood to provision sandbox test keys and a short-lived prod demo key for verification (ETA: 24 business hours once we have contact point).
3) Schedule a 30-minute ops preflight with Redwood infra (suggested: Wed 11/24 or Thu 11/25). Please indicate preferred window.
4) We will enable a temporary higher burst for the first 72 hours to support initial load tests (requires written ack).

Open questions from our side
- Do you require egress / data residency in a specific US region or a dedicated cloud tenancy?
- Any internal security questionnaire items beyond SOC 2 and network egress we should prioritize?

Attachments: pilot-config-template.xlsx, SOW-draft.pdf

Thanks — I’ll follow up in 24 hours with test key details once we have the contact info you send over.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Hosted onramp fastpath: ops agreement & next steps

Alex —

Appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers and asks from our side: 

- We’re fine to start with Hosted to validate performance.
- Data residency: US (primary region us-west). Need confirmation that logs and model traces stay in-region.
- Burst behavior: can you confirm whether burst capacity will be charged at standard per-token rates or treated as a free pilot uplift?
- Security: we’ll need the SOC 2 attestation and a short network diagram for our security team (to share with procurement).

Can you send the sandbox keys to priya@streamlineai.com and I’ll populate the pilot-config template. For the preflight, Thu 11/25 10:00–10:30 PT works for us.

Thanks,
Evan
Head of Product, Streamline.AI
evan.li@streamlineai.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-21T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted onramp fastpath: ops agreement & next steps

Alex / Sean —

Adding quick commercial guidance so our pilot handoff is aligned: 
- Pilot pricing: Hosted pilot is usage-billed at standard per-token rates; for this fastpath we can offer a one-time 30% uplift credit to offset initial test load (applied post-usage).
- If Streamline.AI is comfortable moving to a 12-month reserved commitment, we can present Dedicated pricing that materially reduces per-token cost and includes predictable burst SLAs.
- I’ve attached the pricing-term-sheet.pdf with both pilot credit language and a sample Dedicated term sheet.

I’ll be on the preflight call Thursday.

—Marissa
Account Director | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Evan Li <evan.li@streamlineai.com>
Cc: Priya Raman <priya@streamlineai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted onramp fastpath: ops agreement & next steps

Evan / Priya —

Thanks — short answers below and quick links:

- Data residency: confirmed us-west for logs and traces for the Hosted pilot. We’ll reflect this in the SOW appendix.
- Burst billing: pilot bursts will be covered by the one-time pilot credit (Marissa noted this) — we’ll apply the credit post-trial; normal billing applies after credits are exhausted.
- Security artifacts: SOC 2 attestation and the network diagram are here: https://docs.redwood.ai/soc2-report and https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-1289 (ops diagram).

Sandbox keys: I created two short-lived sandbox keys and emailed them to priya@streamlineai.com (subject line: Redwood sandbox keys — Streamline.AI). Let me know if you don’t receive them by EOD.

Preflight call: Confirmed Thu 2026-11-25 10:00 PT — I scheduled a 30-min slot and sent a calendar invite. Agenda: test plan, burst ramp procedure, canary rollout steps, and success criteria.

Pilot timeline proposal
- Day 0: Sandbox smoke tests (auth, simple generation, KV cache check).
- Day 1–2: Controlled load test with bursts (we’ll monitor latency P95 and error-rate).
- Day 3–5: Canary at 5% → 25% as long as error-rate <1% and 95th latency <500ms for target model.

If this looks good, Priya can send the filled pilot-config-template.xlsx back and we’ll provision prod mapping once we pass the canary.

Best,
Alex
